date_note: Attack on Nov 8, detected Nov 10, fixed Nov 12; users informed Nov 18, which is the date used.
title: Chargemap tells users of data theft via old interface; password hashes may have been extracted
summary: Chargemap says an outsider exploited a flaw in an old technical interface on November 8 to extract user account data, found on November 10 and fixed on November 12. Exposed data includes emails and usernames, and possibly phone numbers, dates of birth and password hashes; payment details are not affected. Next and Cyberattaque.org say no count of affected accounts was given; L'Argus cites 3.5 million users and Security.nl more than 4.1 million app users.
plain: A French EV charging app says hackers took account details, possibly including scrambled passwords, from an old part of its system.
exec: Large user base with reusable credentials; password hashes can be cracked and reused elsewhere.
action: Chargemap users: change your Chargemap password and any other account sharing it, and ignore unsolicited messages claiming to be Chargemap.

validation.note: Next and Cyberattaque.org agree on dates and data; Chargemap's help page returned HTTP 402 and was not read.

review.note: Checked against Next, Cyberattaque.org, Security.nl, L'Argus: dates ok; softened hashes/phone/DOB to possible (sources: may have been extracted, if shared at sign-up); 3.5M and 4.1M are total user figures, now worded so
